solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tap old computer in store

indicators.note: in places the old and computer letters inside the word for a store of goods

parts.note: a store or supply of goods is stock
PC, personal computer

explanation.surface: Someone hides an obsolete computer away in a storeroom by the tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumbing valve that shuts off the water supply is a kind of tap, so the two words are synonyms here.

clue.text: Metal, very thick, contains uranium

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: contains signals that the uranium symbol is held inside the other letters

parts.note: dim means stupid or thick
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A very dense metal has uranium in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick' reads as dense, describing the metal, but it means stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft reactive element, symbol Na, is an alkali metal.

clue.text: Make illegal Open University Disney retrospective

parts.note: OU is the abbreviation for the UK's Open University

indicators.note: retrospective means looking backwards, so the founder's first name is reversed

parts.note: Walt Disney, the animation pioneer

explanation.surface: A university course on Disney's films is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' looks like a film season but turns WALT into TLAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something by law is to prohibit it; the verb sense of this word means exactly that.

clue.text: Din confused arch rival briefly, I gathered

indicators.note: gathered says the single letter I is collected in at the end
confused signals that the letters of arch and the shortened rival are jumbled
briefly means the word rival loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A noisy dispute left one rival confused, the speaker gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' reads as 'I understood', but the I is simply collected at the end after the jumble made by 'confused' from the shortened rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade of banging pots, so the word came to mean a cacophony or din.

clue.text: Building helps to deceive island extroverts

parts.note: to con is to deceive
Crete is a Greek island
mixers are sociable people who mingle easily

explanation.surface: Building work helps fool the outgoing people of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Machines that churn cement on site are aids to construction work, so they help with building.

clue.text: English bug upset Bury

indicators.note: upset in a down-free across clue means the word for a bug is turned back to front

parts.note: a bug is an illness such as flu

explanation.surface: An English insect is disturbed in the town of Bury, in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is a verb; in an across clue 'upset' still means turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury something is to swallow it up or cover it completely, which is what engulfing does.

clue.text: Dope snubs bishop and peer

indicators.note: snubs means rejects, so the abbreviation for bishop is turned away from the word

parts.note: to nobble a racehorse is to drug or dope it
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An idiot ignores a bishop and a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like a fool, but it is the verb for drugging a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the aristocracy, a lord or lady, which is a titled person.

clue.text: Son quits province with one other missing article hidden

indicators.note: quits means leaves, so the abbreviation for son goes from the province's name

parts.note: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: missing means the word other lacks a short word

parts.note: the definite article is the word the

explanation.surface: A son leaves Ulster, and another person goes without a hidden article.
explanation.walkthrough: ULSTER less S gives ULTER; OTHER less THE gives OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is concealed behind a stated one, so the word means secret or hidden.

clue.text: Extremely distant man's entering races with coat on

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, means the coat piece is placed above what follows

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the races abbreviation

parts.note: TT, Tourist Trophy, the motorbike races on the Isle of Man
a man's is a contraction of he is, HE'S

explanation.surface: A man enters motorbike races, wearing a coat, at the farthest venue.
explanation.definitionFit: This superlative means at the greatest distance, so it describes what is most remote.

clue.text: Post agreement

definitions.meaning: letters and mail exchanged between people
a match or similarity between two things

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an exchange of letters and a close match between things.

clue.text: Run into delay? Get off at Crewe maybe

indicators.note: into tells us the abbreviation for run goes inside the word for delay

parts.note: to detain someone is to delay or hold them up
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A rail traveller asks whether they will hit a delay and need to leave the train at Crewe.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is a major railway junction town in the north-west of England, hence 'maybe': it is just one station where you could get off.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a train at a station is the dictionary sense of alighting from the carriage, the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Men perhaps fly spacecraft, say

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers: the men
a fly, such as a horsefly, is an insect that bites: a biter

explanation.surface: Crew members perhaps pilot a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' reads as a verb for piloting, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something circling a planet is an example of a craft in orbit; a spacecraft is one instance, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Taste monosodium a milk contains

indicators.note: contains signals that the letters sit inside the run of words monosodium a milk

explanation.surface: A food scientist notes that a milk product includes monosodium glutamate for flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: This savoury flavour is the fifth basic taste, after sweet, sour, salt and bitter, and is tied to glutamate.

clue.text: Table item army groups found beside Globe

parts.note: RA (Royal Artillery) and RE (Royal Engineers) are two British army corps
the globe is our planet, the Earth

explanation.surface: An item on a table was found next to a globe by army units.
explanation.walkthrough: The table is the periodic table of chemical elements, not furniture; 'found beside' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanide metals are a group of elements listed together on the periodic table under this collective name.

clue.text: Symbol of old order making islanders angry

parts.note: people from the island of Malta are Maltese
cross means annoyed or angry

explanation.surface: An emblem of an ancient knightly order is making the people of some island furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-pointed emblem was the badge of the Knights Hospitaller, an old military order based on Malta.

clue.text: Firm condition stops desperate arranger's job?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: stops means the condition word plugs a gap inside the other word

parts.note: dying for something means being desperate for it
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A firm's stipulation halts a desperate musical arranger's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranger' suggests music, but a codifier arranges laws into a system; the question mark flags that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting laws or rules out in an ordered system is the work of someone who arranges them, so it is an arranger's task.

clue.text: Drink variable amounts to keep old man fit

indicators.note: to keep means the beer word holds the father word inside it

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
pop is an informal word for father, one's old man
x and y are the usual algebraic letters for variable quantities

explanation.surface: Drinking in varying quantities keeps an old man fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' reads as healthy but is the noun for a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack of stroke-like collapse, or a fit of rage, is the sense here: a sudden seizure.

clue.text: Departments suppress occasionally corny cracks

indicators.note: suppress means the departments abbreviation holds down the other letters inside it

parts.note: DEPTS is the abbreviation for departments

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of corny, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Office departments clamp down on a stale joke sometimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' sounds like jokes, matching 'corny', but is a verb for breaking codes.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code is to work out the hidden message, the same as turning ciphertext back into plain text.

clue.text: Ernie selects these elite agents

parts.note: premium means top quality, elite
James Bond is the fictional secret agent, so agents are Bonds

explanation.surface: A man called Ernie handpicks a team of top secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that randomly picks the winning numbers of the UK government savings bonds that pay out prizes instead of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK savings certificates are entered in a monthly prize draw whose winners are chosen by the random number generator named ERNIE.

clue.text: Lawyer deserved to defend Irish revolutionary

indicators.note: to defend means the deserved word wraps around and protects the other letters

parts.note: just means deserved, as in just deserts

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the Irish abbreviation reads backwards

explanation.surface: A lawyer was right to defend an Irish rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal expert, especially a writer on law or a judge, is a jurist, so lawyer is a broad synonym.

clue.text: Fruit almost blankets crown of young fig tree

indicators.note: blankets means the shortened fruit covers the single letter inside it
almost means the fruit word loses its last letter

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

indicators.note: crown of picks the top, the first letter, of young

explanation.surface: A fruit nearly covers the top of a young fig tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BANANA to BANAN; 'blankets' wraps it round Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian tree with aerial roots that grow into new trunks is a species of the Ficus genus, a fig.

clue.text: Did floor for each place old journo added

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
ex means former or old
ED, editor, is a newspaper journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist's job is to lay the floor in every room of an old building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did floor' reads as a decorator's work but means 'baffled', in the sense a puzzle floors you.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to baffle them completely; the past tense sits in the same slot as this past form meaning bewildered.

clue.text: Big successful escapees are at it

definitions.meaning: escaped prisoners still free are said to be at it, the phrase meaning not captured

explanation.definitionFit: The word means big, and the phrase 'at large' describes escapees still on the loose.

clue.text: Local animals often seen accompanying Flora

definitions.text: Local animals often seen accompanying Flora

parts.words: Local animals often seen accompanying Flora
parts.note: the phrase flora and ... pairs a region's plants with its creatures, and Flora reads as a woman's name

explanation.surface: Pets from round about tend to follow a woman named Flora.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective word for the creatures of a region is paired by habit with the word for its plants.

clue.text: Caesar backed theatre in his city

indicators.note: backed signals that the whole assembled run of letters is read in reverse
in places the word for a theatre inside the name of the city

parts.note: Caesar's city is Rome
REP is a repertory theatre

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar supported the theatre in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the whole container round, not just the theatre: build it first, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became the title of Roman rulers, a word that means the ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Top player unwise to sacrifice length with racket

parts.note: the number one player, No 1, written NOI

indicators.note: to sacrifice means to give up a letter from the word for unwise

parts.note: silly means foolish or unwise

explanation.surface: A leading tennis player is foolish to give up length with a racket in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a tennis bat but means din. 'to sacrifice' drops one L from SILLY, leaving SILY.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, so doing something with a racket is doing it loudly.

clue.text: Toadies primarily serve in ME state

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the name of a Middle Eastern country

parts.note: Yemen is a state in the Middle East (ME)

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word serve

explanation.surface: Sycophants serve mainly in some Middle Eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies are flatterers who agree with whatever the boss says, the people who never say no.

clue.text: Boost horse, 18, losing energy

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, which is also known as horse

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the number word

parts.note: eighteen written as a word
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A horse number eighteen in the race is boosted after running out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' looks like a cross-reference to 18 across, but it is simply the number. Losing one E leaves EIGHTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to increase or intensify it, which is the meaning of this verb.
